decisions.reason: The selected design and barista-facing pour-spot orientation necessarily constrain the system layout, but the existing same-message MODIFY records only the general design direction.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: Ok. Let's go with this design. It still keeps alive the DJ Turntables vibe. Let's make the pour spot should be facing the baristas. I want the buttons to be functional and work. Let's try and make it as splash free as possible. Keep the words on the machine the same. Green accents. The only difference is I want it to say "Karla's Matcha Mixer". From the side view I like the thickness of the machine. I want deep matcha wells but I don't want the box to be too big.

value_updates.design_direction: adopt the revised design referenced in the preceding exchange

decisions.reason: The spout design and orientation decision does not alter the independently specified machine name or retained wording.
The pour-spot orientation does not change the independently established green accent color.
The source confirms rather than changes the existing DJ-turntable-inspired visual identity, which is already represented by its own same-message Event.
Spout orientation does not necessarily change the independently specified deep-well bowl form.
The splash-control target is an independent clause already represented by its own same-message Event; the spout orientation decision does not further modify it.
The selected spout geometry and operator orientation do not necessarily alter the basic electrical wiring-plan deliverable.
